subject: anatomy
title: Pleura and lungs: surface markings, hilum and bronchopulmonary segments

steps.tx: The **pleura** is a serous membrane with two layers. The visceral layer covers the lung and is pain insensitive, supplied by autonomic fibres. The parietal layer lines the thoracic wall and is pain sensitive. The costodiaphragmatic recess is the space where the lower pleural reflection lies, and it is the gap that lung tissue does not fill at rest.
steps.say: The pleura is a serous membrane with two layers. The visceral layer covers the lung and is pain insensitive, supplied by autonomic fibres. steps.tx: The **lower border of the lung** lies two ribs above the costodiaphragmatic line. In the midclavicular line the lung reaches the 6th rib, while the pleural line sits at the 8th rib. In the midaxillary line the lung reaches the 8th rib and the pleura reaches the 10th rib. Paravertebrally the pleura reaches the 12th rib.
steps.say: The lower border of the lung lies two ribs above the costodiaphragmatic line. In the midclavicular line the lung reaches the 6th rib, while the pleural line sits at the 8th rib. In the midaxillary line the lung reaches the 8th rib and the pleura reaches the 10th rib. Paravertebrally the pleura reaches the 12th rib.

steps.tx: The **oblique fissure** runs from the spinous process of T3 across the 5th rib in the midaxillary line and then the 6th rib at the midclavicular line. The **right horizontal fissure** runs along the 4th rib to the sternum, separating the middle lobe from the upper lobe. The **lingula** belongs to the left upper lobe and forms the left cardiac border.

vis.alt: Table of surface levels of lung and pleura in ribs: lung reaches rib 6 at the midclavicular line, rib 8 at the midaxillary line and rib 10 posteriorly; pleura reaches rib 8, rib 10 and rib 12 at the same lines.
vis.caption: Lung 6, 8, 10. Pleura 8, 10, 12. The costodiaphragmatic recess lies in the gap.

steps.tx: The **right main bronchus** is shorter, wider and more vertical than the left, so inhaled **foreign bodies** tend to lodge on the right, most often in the middle or lower lobe bronchi. Each **bronchopulmonary segment** is a pyramidal unit supplied by its own segmental bronchus and a tertiary pulmonary artery branch. Its veins run in the intersegmental plane and drain adjacent segments, so it has no independent vein.

Each bronchopulmonary segment is a pyramidal unit supplied by its own segmental bronchus and a tertiary pulmonary artery branch. steps.tx: The **bronchial arteries** arise from the aorta and supply the bronchial tree down to the respiratory bronchioles, plus the lung parenchyma. The **bronchial veins** drain the superficial layer into the azygos on the right and the left superior intercostal or hemiazygos on the left, while deep veins empty into the pulmonary veins. The **pulmonary ligament** is a pleural fold below the hilum. The right tracheobronchial angle is 25 to 30 degrees.
